text:
alex: Heads-up — azure region AZ-East-2 just rolled a network policy update that split firewall zones for tenant peering. We're seeing warm-pool GPU nodes fail to complete keystore handshake (ephemeral keystore) and get stuck in provisioning.

mira: seeing the same in metrics: join rate drops ~40% in east-az1 since ~08:12 UTC. KS logs show 403 on keystore decrypt requests. Not a KMS outage, looks like egress to the keystore proxy is being dropped.

ben: confirmed. Firewall rule change added a default-deny for ephemeral subnets and only allowed privatelink endpoints — our keystore uses a regional LB in the same VNet (no privatelink). Can we add a short-term allow for the keystore LB CIDR? :grimacing:

sam: that would work but it's a config change on infra side. Also curious about audit implications — opening egress will let audit-shipper traffic out of the subnet; retention costs could spike if we backfill logs for the failed joins.

deploy-bot: [AUTOMATION] 1797654321: Canaries in AZ-East-2 -> 5/20 successful node joins, 15/20 failed (keystore handshake). See /infra/canaries/2026-03-21/az-east-2.log

alex: temporary plan: add a narrow egress allow to keystore LB, roll warm-pool join redeploy, monitor join metric for 30m. Longer term we need the keystore behind privatelink or a regional mirror + IAM-bound policy.

mira: +1. Also propose reducing audit backfill retention to avoid cost shock — start with 7d backfill cap and escalate if compliance requires full backfill. Anyone from security on this thread?

ben: cc @security-team (not in channel) — we should document the exception and a timeline (<=24h) for the egress rule. For the keystore itself: moving to privatelink may need TLS/mtls + endpoint ACL changes; that's a 2-week task.

sam: quick workaround command I used in staging (replace with prod CIDR):
```
az network nsg rule create -g rg-infra -n allow-keystore-egress --nsg-name warmpool-nsg --priority 200 --protocol Tcp --destination-address-prefixes 10.45.23.11/32 --destination-port-ranges 443 --access Allow --direction Outbound
```

mira: ran the same in a test subnet, join rate improved to 95% in 10m. If we do this in prod please include monitoring alert to auto-remove rule after 12h if stable.

alex: I'll coordinate the prod change with infra ops. Action items:
- alex: request short-lived egress allow and deploy warm-pool redeploy (now)
- ben: draft exception ticket + timeline for security review (1h)
- mira: monitor join metrics + prepare rollback automation (12h)
- sam: start privatelink design doc (ETA 2w)

sam: FYI cost note — if we end up backfilling audit logs for the failed nodes, estimate ~80GB/day of additional logs -> +$2k/week at current tier. Flagging for finance.

ben: added ticket INF-7623 with exception details and cost note. Linking to canary logs and keystore audit lines.

alex: rolling prod NSG change in 2m. Will post status. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: [AUTOMATION] 1797654338: Infra change pushed: allow-keystore-egress created on warmpool-nsg (prod-east-az1).

mira: join rate now 93% and climbing. Keystore handshake errors down to baseline. Leaving monitors on.

ben: thanks team. Once security signs off we can keep the narrow rule for up to 24h then remove and continue working on privatelink path.

alex: closing thread when exception ticket accepted. If anything regresses ping me directly.
